_meta.description: Source roadmap shown on the dashboard: what each platform costs, what it takes to turn on, and what it actually returns. Cost figures are grounded in measured runs where possible - see 'basis' on each entry.
_meta.measured_baseline: One live YouTube run on 2026-08-28: 6 queries -> 27 videos -> 2,210 comments -> 127 relevant, for 627 of 10,000 daily quota units.

sources.name: YouTube
sources.cost_detail: 10,000 quota units/day. A search costs 100, a page of 100 comments costs 1.
sources.basis: Measured: 2,210 comments for 627 units — roughly 35,000 comments/day within the free quota.
sources.reads: Public comments + replies on ANY video
sources.verdict: The workhorse. Only free source that reads other people's comments at category scale, and Indonesian food content on it is plentiful.

sources.name: Reddit
sources.cost_detail: OAuth 'script' app is free forever. 100 queries/minute, no daily cap.
sources.basis: Estimated: 6 queries + ~60 posts ≈ 66 requests ≈ 40 seconds of a 100/min budget. Client self-throttles to ~92/min.
sources.setup: Create a free script app (~2 min)
sources.reads: Full nested comment trees on ANY public post
sources.verdict: Code is written and tested. Free, but Indonesian food discussion on Reddit is thin — expect English, global, category-level signal rather than local market evidence.

sources.name: Threads
sources.cost_detail: No usage fee, but the 'threads_keyword_search' permission requires Meta app review.
sources.basis: Not measured — this module is unverified against the live API.
sources.setup: Meta app + OAuth + app review (hours to weeks)
sources.reads: Top-level posts matching a keyword. CANNOT read replies to other people's posts.
sources.verdict: Structurally weak for this tool: it returns posts mentioning your keywords, not conversation about them. The reply data we actually want is unreachable for accounts you don't own.

sources.name: X / Twitter
sources.cost_detail: $0.005 per post read. No free tier since Feb 2026; credits must be bought up front.
sources.basis: Calculated: 2,210 posts (matching our measured YouTube haul) × $0.005 = $11.05. Weekly runs ≈ $44/month.
sources.verdict: Not recommended. Real money for thinner data — X skews news/politics in Indonesia, not groceries. Not built.

sources.name: Instagram / TikTok
sources.cost_detail: APIs are free but read only accounts you own.
sources.setup: Graph API on Zorvex's own account
sources.reads: Only Zorvex's OWN posts and their replies
sources.verdict: Where the audience actually is, and unreachable for competitors without scraping. Worth wiring up for Zorvex's OWN account once they post — a separate, easy integration.

sources.name: Tokopedia / Shopee
sources.verdict: The uncomfortable gap: this is where Zorvex's actual buyers will review the product. Only route is scraping, which we won't ship.

next_builds.title: YouTube video + channel enrichment
next_builds.cost: Free — ~2 extra quota units per run
next_builds.detail: videos.list and channels.list return view counts, tags, and creator subscriber counts (1 unit per 50 items). Lets leads be weighted by actual reach instead of counted equally, and produces a ranked creator table — the influencer-scoring data Option A originally wanted.

next_builds.title: Reddit activation
next_builds.detail: Add REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET to .env, run check_reddit.py, then --source youtube reddit. Broadens category evidence; will not add Indonesian depth.

next_builds.title: Instagram Graph API on Zorvex's own account
next_builds.detail: Once Zorvex's Instagram has comment volume, their own-channel replies are readable through the official API with no scraping. Directly measures their own audience rather than the category.

next_builds.title: Claude-assisted analyzer
next_builds.detail: pip install anthropic + an API key. Catches sarcasm and emoji-carried sentiment the lexicon misses — e.g. a comment scored neutral despite 🤦😒 markers. Run it once on the final dataset to check how far off the rules baseline was.
